summary: Apply both blocking findings: add pre-commit protection for staged other-flow flow.json files and pin post-merge worktree metadata writes to the selected spec id.

items.title: Post-commit dirty detection cannot prevent committing staged other-flow metadata
items.rationale: The finding identifies a concrete ownership violation: a staged other-flow flow.json could be included in the target finalize commit before any post-cleanup warning scan runs.
items.evidence: src/flow/lib/run-finalize-cleanup.js runTeardown stages the target flow.json then calls git commit. spec.json currently requires post-cleanup detection but does not require a pre-commit safeguard for already-staged non-target specs/*/flow.json paths.

items.title: R1 does not pin the actual cross-flow mutation integration path
items.rationale: The finding points to the likely root path from Issue #345: after worktree authority switches to the main repo, an unbound FlowManager can resolve another active flow in the main repo and mutate its flow.json.
items.evidence: src/flow/lib/flow-context.js uses baseFlowManager.forRoot(mainRoot) when the main repo flow.json exists, without binding specId. spec.json R1 currently requires generic current-flow writes but does not name the post-merge worktree authority-switch scenario.
